description: A rolling audio buffer one beat long, recorded continuously from the input and played back from wherever an automation voltage points, in mono or stereo

params.text: Sets the tempo of the internal clock, 1 to 400 BPM, and with it the buffer length, which is one beat
Chooses what the automation voltage means: direct sets the playback position outright, wrap adds an offset onto a loop already running at the tempo
Switches the clock from the BPM knob to the STEP or PHASE input
Crossfades the output from the buffer read at the recording position fully left to the buffer read at the automation position fully right

inputs.text: A rising edge past 1V sets the tempo from the time since the previous edge and restarts the buffer, and is read only while EXTERNAL is on
A rising edge past 1V restarts the clock and the buffer from the beginning
A clock given as a rising ramp: a jump of more than 0.5V sets the tempo from the time since the last jump; it is read only while EXTERNAL is on and STEP is unpatched
A rising edge past 1V fills the buffer with silence
The audio recorded into the buffer, mono or the left channel
Sets the playback position, 0 to 10V covering the whole buffer and wrapping round outside that
Shifts the dry-wet mix, 1V covering the whole of the DRY/WET knob's travel, although the manual describes this jack as 0-10V
The right channel recorded into the buffer; patching it puts the module into stereo

outputs.text: The mixed buffer playback, mono or the left channel
The right channel of the buffer playback

notes: with EXTERNAL on and neither STEP nor PHASE patched the clock is reset every sample, so nothing plays back
the buffer holds exactly one beat, so changing the tempo changes its length; an item on the panel menu sets whether what is recorded is resampled to fit or trimmed and padded
the display draws the buffer with a red line at the recording position and a yellow line at the playback position, and the number at the top is the tempo
a BufferSludgerTransposer placed on either side of this module adds its own automation to the automation input
menu: Load WAV File — opens a file dialog and reads a WAV file into the buffer
Interpolation Mode: None, Linear, Cubic, Optimal 2x, Optimal 8x, Optimal 32x — chooses how a sample between two buffer positions is worked out
Disable Output Filter — turns off the 20kHz lowpass on the outputs
Disable Anti Clicking Filter — turns off the short crossfade applied when the playback position jumps a long way
Enable speed change on bpm change — resamples what is already in the buffer when the tempo changes, instead of trimming it or padding it with silence
Visual Mode: Disable, Samples, Disk — chooses how the buffer is drawn
Ui Downsampling — sets how many samples are skipped when the buffer is drawn, 1 to 64; higher values draw faster and more coarsely
